authoring.value:
Notice that $f(x,y)$ equals zero when $x=0$ and $y=0.$ These lines divide the $xy$-plane into four regions, as shown below. Since we have an "or equal to" inequality, we use solid lines to divide the plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14004890/assets/c44c38febc908fe5e941978bf44bab2e2cb4bd250765950d84f9294c9c4c9c4b.png)

To determine the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14004890/assets/209576cd78e9beb1c0f7a9bce8267163df1668a830ffc5c06918f8a726600fbe.png)

Next, we calculate the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region using a sign table:

|  | Test point | $-7x$ | $y$ | $f(x,y)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top-left | $(-1,1)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| Top-Right | $(1,1)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Bottom-Left | $(-1,-1)$ | $+$ | $-$ | $-$ |
| Bottom-Right | $(1,-1)$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |

 

Finally, on our diagram, we shade in the solutions to $f(x,y)\le 0$ using the *last* column of the table above.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14004890/assets/cf7fdbafdf968d3e6adfe9544a3b9e5e1736ce22fc808567f1d66fc80916534e.png)
